turns.content: A student inserted exactly six extra digits into the numerator of 1/N and obtained 0.0 overline{0231846597}. How long was the original repetend, and how is it embedded in the displayed block?

Let r be the original repetend length obtained above and B the numerical value of that retained block. Express 0.0 overline{B} as a fraction in terms of r, and state the divisibility condition required for it to equal 1/N.
Confirm the denominator in that fraction, paying particular attention to the one nonrepeating zero before the r-digit repetend.
Once r is known, factor the resulting denominator. Use the fact that the displayed ten-digit block has no repeated digit to rule out any denominator factor that cannot occur in the retained block.
Search the order-preserving r-position subsequences of 0231846597 for block values satisfying the divisibility condition. Explain why the retained digits need not be contiguous.
Identify the unique original r-digit repetend and reduce its fraction over the derived denominator.
